questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The tigress that was killed by the villagers was not only a man-eater, ________ a mother.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **but also**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Not only"** and **"but also"** are **correlative conjunctions**.
 
• The phrase **"not only"** is typically paired with **"but also"** to indicate the inclusion of two related elements.
 
• Using **"but also"** emphasizes that the tigress had dual roles: a man-eater and a mother.

Correct sentence: *The tigress that was killed by the villagers was not only a man-eater, **but also** a mother*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (but):** "But" alone does not correctly follow "not only" and fails to convey the duality of the tigress's roles.
 
• **Option 3 (and):** "And" is not used in the "not only... but also" structure and would disrupt the grammatical flow.
 
• **Option 4 (but often):** "But often" changes the meaning and does not complete the "not only" structure.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Serena _________ from fever since the 5th of this month.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the **present perfect continuous tense** because it **describes** an action that started in the past and is still continuing.
 
• The **correct form of the verb **to use in this case is** "has been suffering".**
 
• This** tense** is used to talk about actions that began in the past and are still continuing at the present moment.
 
• Example: *She **has been living** in London since 1995.*

Hence, the correct statement is: ***Serena has been suffering__ from fever since the 5th of this month*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The present perfect continuous tense is often used with time expressions such as** "since" and "for".**
 
• **"Since"** is used to indicate the starting point of the action, while** "for"** is used to indicate the duration.
 
• Example with **"for":** *He **has been working** here **for** three years.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Prem is an excellent chess player. He is the ______ student of the class too.
questions.solution:
The correct option is: **1) most intelligent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is structured to convey that Prem is not just intelligent but the most intelligent in the entire class.
 
• This means that out of all the students, Prem stands out as the one with the highest degree of intelligence.
 
• When we are comparing more than two things or expressing the extreme degree of a particular quality, we use the **superlative form of the adjective**.
 
 
• **Example: **Among all the athletes, John is the most skilled.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this question, **"Most intelligent"** indicates that Prem is at the highest level of intelligence compared to all other students in the class.

Hence, the correct answer is: *Prem is an excellent chess player. He is the **most intelligent**__ student of the class too.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Why Other Options Are Incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 2:** **intelligently **– This is an adverb, and it modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. The sentence needs an adjective to describe Prem, not an adverb. So "intelligently" would not be grammatically appropriate.
 
• **Option 3: intelligent **– This is the positive form of the adjective. It only describes Prem as being intelligent but doesn't convey the idea that he is the best or most intelligent in comparison to others. It lacks the superlative quality that is essential for the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 4:** **more intelligent** – This is the comparative form, used to compare two things or people. The sentence, however, is not comparing Prem to one other person but rather stating that Prem is the top student among all others. So, the comparative form is inappropriate here.

questions.question:

__
 
• Rules for question tag:

 
 
• The sentence and the question tag must be in the same tense.
 
• For the negative question tag, use the contracted form of 'helping verb' and 'not.'
 
• If the sentence is positive, the question tag must be negative and vice-versa.
 
• Always use pronouns in the question tag.
 
 
• Example*: didn't, haven't, doesn't​*
 
 
 
 
 
• *​​*Correct sentence__: *The Health Minister has been discharged from the hospital, **hasn't **he?*

__
 
• A tag question is a special construction in English.
 
• It is a statement followed by a mini-question.
 
• We use tag questions to ask for confirmation.
 
• They mean something like: *"Is that right?" or "Do you agree?"*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__** *

questions.question:

When I solved the sum ______, I was very happy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'myself'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us explore the given options__:

 __
 
• The pronoun 'oneself' is **used as the object of a verb or preposition when this is the same as the subject of the clause and the subject is stated or understood as ‘one’**.
 
• The pronoun 'herself' is **used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to a female person or animal previously mentioned as the subject of the clause**.
 
• The pronoun 'myself' is **used by a speaker to refer to himself or herself as the object of a verb or preposition when he or she is the subject of the clause**.
 
• The pronoun 'itself' is **used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to a thing or animal previously mentioned as the subject of the clause**.

 
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Complete Sentence__: *When I solved the sum **myself,** I was very happy*.

questions.question:
Select the correct pair of words for the blanks in the given sentence.

________ are the prime resource of a country and a tea is served in a _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"cattle; kettle".**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Let's go through each option:**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Chinese leader's formal Chinese suit ______ Changpao.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. is called. 

The sentence can be considered as “The Chinese leader's formal Chinese suit is called Changpao (by someone).” 

 
• This sentence is written in the passive voice.
 
• The passive voice is used when we want to focus attention on the person or thing affected by the action, here the thing is the Chinese suit.

The active voice will be “(Someone) calls(simple present tense) the Chinese leader’s formal suit Changpao.” 

 
• We use the simple present tense for anything that is factual.
 
• When active verb is in the simple present tense (calls), we make passive verb forms with is/am/are + past participle form of the verb (is called). 

​Other options are incorrect because:

 
• Option 1- ​‘Call’ is a base verb and base form of verbs can only be directly used after 

 
 
• modal auxiliaries like can, may, must, would, should, could etc.
 
• Why- eg: Why stay? 
 
 
 
• Option 2- According to the Subject-Verb Agreement rule, the subject and verb must agree in number. This means both need to be singular or both need to be plural.
 
 
• ‘Formal Chinese suit’ is a singular subject. 
 
• So the verb that accompanies it must be singular too. 
 
 
 
• Option 3- ‘Will be called Changpao’ means that the name has not been given to the formal suit yet, and this will happen in the future. This is wrong as this piece of clothing was introduced to China during the Qing dynasty (17th–20th centuries).

• Now, let's explain why the other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **"Flush" - **This term is usually used to describe the action of cleaning out a system, such as pipes or a toilet, by causing a large amount of water to flow through it. It's not typically used in the context of preparing water for drinking.
 
• **"Flirt" -** This is a social and sometimes romantic behavior that involves speaking and behaving in a way that suggests a playful attraction to someone, typically not involving serious intentions. It's not related to the context of drinking water.
 
• **"Flicker" - **This term usually refers to a light or a flame that shines or burns in an unsteady, changeable way. It's not relevant to the action of preparing water for drinking.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.**

Meteorologists are still ______ to understand sting jets.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **working**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the present continuous tense, indicating an ongoing action.
 
• "**Working**" is the present participle form of the verb "**work**", which is the appropriate form to use in this context.
 
• The sentence could also be written as "*Meteorologists are still trying to understand sting jets*", with a similar meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

**Complete sentence: ***Meteorologists are still working __to understand sting jets.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: "**on work**", is **incorrect **as it is not a grammatically correct phrase. It should be "at work" or "working".
 
• Option 3: "**worked**", is **incorrect **as it is in the past tense, indicating a completed action. This does not fit with the present continuous tense of the sentence.
 
• Option 4: "**works**", is **incorrect **as it is in the present tense, indicating a habitual or general truth. This does not fit with the ongoing nature of the action in the sentence.

- Option 2, "done a lot of", is incorrect because it is the past participle form of the verb "do", not the simple past tense form needed in this sentence.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The teacher assured: “You have completed your homework, __________?”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the question, the teacher is asking for confirmation, which requires a question tag at the end of the sentence.
 
• The main clause is positive (**you have completed**), so the question tag should be** negative.**
 
• Therefore, the correct question tag is "haven't you".

Hence, the correct statement is **"*The teacher assured: “You have completed your homework, haven't you?__”*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Question tags are used to seek confirmation and are generally the opposite form of the main clause (**positive main clause has negative question tag and vice versa).**

 
 
• **Example:** *She is coming, **isn't she?***
 
 
 
• If the main clause is negative, the question tag will be positive.
 
 
• **Example:** *He isn't coming, **is he?***
